_comment: Layout constants that are not expressible inside the Anchor IDL. Account lengths are byte-exact and double as getProgramAccounts dataSize filters, so a drift here is a silent empty scan — test/idl.test.mjs re-derives every length from the IDL type definitions and fails if this file disagrees.

reserveWidths._comment: The launch reserve: zero bytes appended pre-deploy that future fields are carved from, front-first, so accountLens never move. Deployer has had 26 bytes carved (btc_share_bps u16 + epoch_units_bought u64 + btc_units_bought u64 + user_flags u64).

flags._comment: Bit INDICES into WkConfig.flags (u64). The flag value is 1n << index. PAUSED_DEPLOY is an INCIDENT-ONLY deploy halt since v2: it stops money going in while settle/claim/withdraw keep running (withdraw-under-halt is pinned by program test), and it is never a product pause — routine operator maintenance is stopping the crank, and a user pausing themselves is a control-plane row the crank honors.

userFlags._comment: Bit INDICES into Deployer.user_flags (u64) — the switches a USER owns, moved only by set_user_flags(mask, value) signed by the manager authority. An operator can never write them. The value is 1n << index, and 0 is always the pre-existing behaviour. PAUSE_MINING is LEGACY as of v2: the program no longer reads it (pause is operator policy; the deploy path executes whatever the crank sends), but the bit stays settable and the CRANK is expected to keep honoring a set bit as 'paused' until the frontend stops writing it — a user's standing instruction must not be dropped by the upgrade. HOLD_VAULT_BUYS still gates BOTH ticket legs on chain so hashrate banks on the Miner; it does not stop claim_sats, which is money owed to the user. HOLD_SATS still gates claim_sats (enforced only when the caller passes the Deployer as the fifth remaining account; the position's own authority overrides — the force-sweep). A mask touching any bit not listed here is rejected with BadSetting.

remainingAccounts._comment: Per-user remaining_accounts, in order, for the batch instructions whose shape the IDL cannot express — an IDL describes named accounts, and these are a repeating run appended after them. Transcribed from the program source (claim.rs) and verified against the deployed program by simulation, NOT inferred. Only wk_claim_sats_batch is published here because only its shape has been proven both ways; the other batch instructions have a single fixed stride and are not yet published rather than being guessed at.

wk_claim_sats_batch._comment: FOUR or FIVE accounts per user, and the choice is the caller's. Four is what every client deployed before 2026-08-20 sends and it still works exactly as it did — the upgrade could not require five without failing every live caller from the moment it landed. Five adds the position's Deployer, which is the account carrying user_flags, and is what lets the program see HOLD_SATS at all: a four-account call cannot read the flag so it claims for a holder regardless. Any other multiple is refused with BadRemainingAccounts (6021). Passing another position's Deployer is refused with BadPda (6003), so a caller cannot choose which switch to read. The signer matters: when the signer IS the position's own authority the hold is ignored and the claim proceeds — that is the force-sweep, and it needs no separate instruction.

seeds._comment: PDA seed recipes, in order. kind=literal is UTF-8 bytes of value; kind=pubkey is the named account's 32 bytes; u16le/u32le/u64le are the named argument little-endian.

reservedUnusedParams._comment: Param slots the program STOPPED reading in the thin-wrapper upgrade (v2). Indexes are a stable ABI and never shift; the seeded values remain as reference numbers an operator may copy into its own off-chain config. 7 (HASHRATE_TILE_COEFF) was already unread before v2; 10/11/16 fed the on-chain ticket-split engine (epoch knee, dust threshold, bootstrap floor), which is operator ticket policy in the crank now.

itemShapes._comment: The v2 batch-instruction item structs, byte-exact. Borsh: little-endian, vec = u32 length prefix + items. The instruction DISCRIMINATORS did not change in v2 (Anchor sighash is name-only); only these arg bodies did, which is why an old client against the new program fails borsh decode loudly — the intended atomic-cutover failure mode. DeployItem.amount must be >= MIN_DEPLOY_AMOUNT, <= MAX_PER_ROUND_AMOUNT (per shard, 0 disables), divisible by popcount(tile_mask), and must fit the user's max_per_round meter; tile_mask needs popcount within [MIN_TILE_COUNT, MAX_TILE_COUNT] and bits within TILE_TOTAL. BuyTicketItem.tickets is WHOLE TICKETS (1 ticket = 100 hashrate units) and must fit the miner's spendable hashrate. Violations are per-item skips (WkDeploySkipped/WkTicketsSkipped), never batch failures — except a duplicated shard, which reverts whole with DuplicateAuthId.

maxPerRound._comment: v2 reinterprets Deployer byte offset 107 (was per_round_amount, the exact bet the program divided) as max_per_round: the ceiling on the round's TOTAL stake across all the user's shards, enforced by the last_round/staked_in_round meter, skip-never-clamp. The DeployerSettings WIRE field keeps the name per_round_amount for client compatibility and lands in this slot.

satrush._comment: Sat Rush is a third-party program WhiteKnight CPIs into. Sizes were verified against live mainnet accounts of every type; its upgrade authority can redeploy at any time, so clients must length-check before decoding and halt on mismatch rather than read shifted fields.
